newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: NWE oil products steady to firm, mogas calmer.
newsitem.headline: NWE oil products steady to firm, mogas calmer.

text.p: NWE oil products were steady to firm after some initial weakness, gasoline calmer after frenetic trading on Thursday, dealers said.

Gasoline traded once at $182.50 fob Rotterdam in early trading, but was subsequently offered higher, at around $184/$185 fob. Traders said the later offers, although higher than late on Thursday, were more in line with swaps levels.
Given the rapid fluctuations on Thursday, traders said it was hard to determine whether the market was steady or firmer.
"It really depends which particular moment (on Thursday) you're comparing with," one trader said.
Arbitrage to the United States remained viable.

Heating oil barges were broadly steady. IPE August futures ticked up, but premiums came off to IPE August +$1.25 fob Rotterdam. Traders said sellers had realised that no buyers were prepared to pay as high as +$2.
One barge traded this morning at August +75 cents fob Rotterdam.

High sulphur fuel oil, which moved out of this week's $85/$86 fob Rotterdam range late on Thursday, pushed $1 a tonne higher. One barge traded early at $85.50, but by mid-morning $87 had been done. Late morning offers were at $87.50.

Bunker demand was low after high activity on Thursday. Traders said some suppliers still had shorts to cover, corresponding to bunkers already sold. -- Philip Blenkinsop, Amsterdam Newsroom, +31 20 504 5004
